title: AI Website Builder vs a Template
metaDescription: Templates and AI builders solve the same problem differently. An honest comparison of what each is actually good at, and how to choose.
body: Buying a template and describing a site to an AI are two answers to the same question: how do I get a decent website without hiring anyone. They fail in different places. Here's where each one is actually better, written by people with an obvious stake in one of them — so weigh it accordingly and check the claims.
The core difference
A template is a finished design you fill in. Someone made every layout decision in advance; your job is to replace their content with yours and adjust what the editor lets you adjust.
An AI builder makes the layout decisions per site, from a description. Nothing is chosen in advance, which is both the advantage and the risk.
Where a template wins

• You can see it before you commit. This is the biggest one and it's not close. You browse, you find one you like, you know exactly what you're getting. With an AI builder you write a description and hope.
  • Predictability. Templates were designed by a person who considered the edge cases, tested them on real devices, and shipped. A generated design is new each time, and new means unverified.
  • Images are handled. Template ecosystems assume photography and give you somewhere to put it. This is a hard limit on Kodely specifically: generated sites contain no photographs at all, because published sites can't load anything from another host. If your site is photo-driven, a template ecosystem is simply the better tool.
  • Complete features. Templates usually come attached to a platform with a store, a booking system, forms that deliver, and a CMS. Kodely has none of those. Here's the full list of what it can't do.
Where an AI builder wins

• Nothing to fight. Templates resist. Your business has five services and the template has three slots; your key selling point is a price list and the template wants a photo gallery. Half the work of a template is bending your business into someone else's structure. A generated design starts from your description, so the sections are the sections you asked for.
  • Changes are a sentence. "Move the price list above the about section, make the headings larger, take the green warmer." With a template you go and find the setting — assuming the setting exists.
  • You don't start from a blank page. Choosing between four hundred templates is its own kind of paralysis. Describing your business is easier than evaluating a catalogue.
  • The result is yours specifically. A template that looks great is a template a thousand other businesses also bought.
What Kodely does about the predictability problem
The honest weakness of any AI builder is that you can't see it before you commit. Three things address that here:

Enhance. Type one line, press Enhance, and you get a structured brief back — audience, goal, tone, sections in order, key content — which you read and edit before anything is built. It's free and never charged as a build, because a preview you pay for isn't a preview.

Nothing charged for broken output. Every build is genuinely compiled on our servers. If it doesn't compile, it gets one automatic repair attempt, and if it still doesn't, the build is charged zero credits.

Free rollback. Every successful build is a checkpoint. Restoring an earlier one costs nothing — it restores a snapshot rather than generating anything — so an experimental edit is genuinely low-stakes.
What you own at the end
Templates vary enormously here and it's worth checking before you buy. Some are HTML files that are yours; some only exist inside one platform's editor and cannot leave it.

With Kodely the answer is fixed: your project is a Vite + React + TypeScript + Tailwind application, you can read the source in the Code tab, and you can download the whole thing as a zip for free, any number of times. It's a standard project — npm install, npm run build, host it anywhere. More on what "real code" should mean.
A straightforward way to choose

Pick a template if: your site depends on photography; you need a store, bookings, a working contact form, or a CMS; you want to see exactly what you're getting before you commit; or someone non-technical needs to edit it regularly.

Pick an AI builder if: you need one strong page rather than a structure; your content doesn't fit standard slots; you'd rather describe your business than evaluate four hundred designs; or you want the underlying code to be genuinely portable.

Honestly, try both. They're cheap to evaluate. Kodely gives you 750 credits free with no card, which is enough to see a real first build and decide whether the result is better than the template you were considering. If it isn't, buy the template — that's a perfectly good outcome.
